Case reproduction number (Rc) by true origin

Source: R/transmission.R
rc_by_origin.Rd

The mean number of secondary cases each case caused, by the case's true origin. A case is a blood-stage clone onset, a row of classify_cases(); its secondary cases are the targets of its links in transmission_links(), infected by a bite's blood stage or by a relapse of the batch the bite left.

Usage

rc_by_origin(
  run,
  unit = c("episode", "acquisition"),
  kind = c("all", "direct", "liver"),
  from = 0,
  followup = 0
)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

unit

"episode" or "acquisition": what a case is (see Details).

kind

"all", "direct" or "liver": the links counted, as in transmission_links().

from

count the cases that began on day from or later.

followup

count the cases that began on day SIM_DAYS - followup or earlier.

Value

a data.table, one row per origin, every origin present: origin (a factor of the origins classify_cases() gives, without "recrudescence" for unit = "acquisition"), n_cases (integer), n_secondary (the sum of the cases' link weights), Rc (n_secondary / n_cases) and onward_frac (the share of cases with a secondary case), the last two NA with no case. To pool runs, divide the summed n_secondary by the summed n_cases.

Details

Cases. With unit = "episode" every clone onset is a case, a recrudescence included. With unit = "acquisition" a recrudescence is not a case: its onward transmission is credited to the clone it re-expanded from, through repeated recrudescences, so each acquisition has one count. A subpatent holder's transmission is credited to the case that began it. Founders infect, but are not cases.

Secondary cases. Each secondary case counts once: one from an outcrossed oocyst credits 1/2 to each parent. A bite that delivers two genotypes gives two secondary cases. Masked relapses count like any other; join classify_cases() on the links to leave them out. kind = "direct" and kind = "liver" add up to kind = "all".

The end of the run. A case near the end has had less time to transmit, above all through relapses: a hypnozoite stays dormant 1 / (ALPHA_ACTIVATE + MU_HYPNOZOITE) days on average, about four months at the defaults, and more than a year for 1 in 20. followup counts only the cases that began at least that many days before SIM_DAYS. A run that went extinct is not censored.

The phase of the epidemic. Rc reflects the phase the counted cases began in: above 1 while an epidemic grows from its founders, near 1 at a self-sustaining steady state, and lower where imports sustain transmission. To compare runs, choose from and followup inside a stretch that plot_diagnostics() shows to be steady; followup alone keeps a growing run's early cases.

References

Fraser C (2007) Estimating individual and household reproduction numbers in an emerging epidemic. PLoS ONE 2(8): e758. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0000758

See also

transmission_links(), classify_cases()

Examples

rc_by_origin(example_run(), from = 100, followup = 100)
#>               origin n_cases n_secondary       Rc onward_frac
#>               <fctr>   <int>       <num>    <num>       <num>
#> 1:          imported       9         0.0 0.000000   0.0000000
#> 2: local reinfection      35        50.5 1.442857   0.3714286
#> 3:           relapse      67        81.0 1.208955   0.2985075
#> 4:     recrudescence       3         0.0 0.000000   0.0000000
